reviews.review:
An unapologetic Left 4 Dead clone - but all in the right ways.

Devs showing strong mod support (sweet).

Audio design is great. It has voice acting thats actually not terrible, the music fits pretty well and fits the games style.

Gameplay is stable for the most part, there is definitely something going on within the engine when there are tons of infected on screen, but I believe this is going to be addressed (this is Early Access).

I would like to see more weapons, but I imagine this is coming. The guns do feel good to shoot, and I am a fan of the secondary SFX (maybe a Magnum variant to match the Burst Fire one in the future?)

Not a "full-price" game. Can't beat that. 

Its Left 4 Dead... 
but it takes place in the 70s, in the future, in space (rad).
So, it´s literally L4D in space, in the 70s !!!

An Ambitious game trying the same formula as the Left 4 Dead series.

There are several reviews already highlighting the fact that this retro style is what makes the game standout from the original Left 4 Dead but also is also the reason the game lacks a little something to the mix. The audio does feel subdued, as if the scenario is no that life threatening to the cast. There is a bit of immersion break as well.

Granted, Anacrusis has a lot of potential, with the Devs being reactive to feedback and reviews. Thus its still worth taking a look at the game along the way, and if possible to help support the devs by buying the game early. Here's hoping it does hit the right formula for its own niche.

Let me be blunt:  I did not like this game.  But I don't think that's the game's fault.  It's not perfect but it's pretty decent, all told, and I think maybe you might like it.

Whether you like it or not you can judge by this elevator pitch:  Left 4 Dead's gameplay, more-or-less, with the visuals of the 1970s and the hokey laser-pew optimism of the Flash Gordon 50s.

Let me tell you more.  But let me be honest with you, I hate the 1970s.  People thought it was a good idea to paint everything various orangey/browny tones, put lead in gasoline, get excited over four-tonne cars with 100 HP engines and smoke cigarettes around their children at all hours of the day.  The 70s are stupid, I'm glad they're gone.

But it does make for a coherent visual look that isn't the endless rusty metal grimdark broken concrete of the modern zombie shooter, and having a tight, coherent look goes a long way, it really does.

Granted, nothing in the game looked scary.  Nobody in the game ever really sounded scared either.  Sometimes the player characters sounded a bit sarcastic when they weren't excited, and that's fine!  When you've got laser-pew blasters and such, and everything's brightly coloured, you may as well embrace it whole-heartedly.  Frankly, if I have another grimdark zombie extravaganza I may just puke, so I'm okay with all this.

But that does also take the visceral edge off.  Left 4 Dead was intense, and a good chunk of that was Mike Patton's insane vocalizations and all the yellin' and hollarin' the player characters did.  This game is missing that.  It's trying for that energy and intensity of Left 4 Dead, but without the audio, something is missing.  Something important is missing.

The game gets kind of stuttery in a way when you're swarmed by a lot of zomboids.  I think they're trying to convey the zombies are busy flailing at you, but it just feels like physics errors or something.  And maybe the pacing of chapter 1's finale is really off, since it's just a relentless slog through little zombies for a few minutes with essentially no breaks.  The occasional little pause would have gone a long way.

But that's basically it, and that's a tuning issue.  So why didn't I like it?  Well.. I found myself constantly panning around, trying to see where my fellow players were, wishing they'd stick closer, wishing they'd look behind them more, wishing I'd not been left in a hallway, and quelling my urge to be some kind of barky-orders squad leader the whole while.  I don't mind doing it at all, but it takes a different sort of player to agree to it than my pals, and I don't want to subject them to it.

So I found my experience nerve-wracking, in a way.  Not strictly because of the game, but because I found myself trying to track every last monster AND my allies all at once.  In my ideal world, they'd kind of form up around me, each watching a quadrant, communicating what they're doing, etc., etc.  They didn't know I wanted that, and I didn't tell them I wanted that, and that's unfair to them.

So we played one chapter over the free weekend, and I was like, "Thanks!  I've had enough!"  They had fun and praised the visuals, and I was just trying to unjangle my nerves.

(And yet I didn't call the game intense.  I'm weird, I know.)

So I didn't buy the game in the end.  I might get convinced later, it's not impossible, but I don't know anybody who'd play it the way I'd want to, and it's not something you can play solo.  So I have to pass.  But that doesn't mean it's not for you, so maybe YOU should.

This game looks to be super cool! kind of like an alternate version of Left4dead. I played it on the free weekend and beat it in an evening with a friend. I understand this is early release and theyre developing more content but 30 dollars base and even 15 on sale is a steep tag for what felt like 3-4 hours of content. Was fun over the free weekend but not yet compelled to make a purchase. Maybe the main issue is this game feels a bit too much like Left 4 Dead, almost like it was originally a mod, with many of the exact same weapon types, grenades, and mechanics taken nearly straight from it. There's a few unique ideas but I would like a -lot- of unique ideas that don't end up manifesting as a bloat of power weapons. Definitely needs more polish and a fix for the lag during big events.

I am optimistic for it though. Hopefully it can stand out as its own and not end up as as a bootleg clone down the road.

Needs to be a permanent option, the ai-controlled mates are so fun to play with.

As someone who has played far to much Left 4 Dead I was super hopeful for this game (as I was for Back 4 Blood). 

I played this during the free weekend during Early Access. The devs have a road map to full release later this year, but atm it very much feels like Early Access, though all the issues I have are something that can and may be fixed before release.

Pros
• I really liked the aesthetic and art design. 
• The locations and bits of story you get are also great. 
• Potential for co-op content
• Events require two people to trigger so people can only run so far ahead and can't troll trigger an event

Cons
• Guns and items options are limited (you have your basic SMG, shotgun, and rifle + 3 special weapons).
• There is little reason to explore.
• AI director never made a run feel consistently difficult. Was either on 1 or 11. 
• Perks don't have much of a feel to them
• the "melee" push bubble thing is inconsistent and anemic
• No PVP/VS mode


There is little reason to explore. There aren't very many things to look at and even less pickups to find. Finding the Matter Compilers to get new perks is the main thing to look for, but in a typical run I was finding only 9 out of 12 perks and never really felt a need to look around for more. The guns, ammo, and grenades on the main route were almost always more than enough as they are mostly only needed during an event. Special aliens didn't spawn very much outside of events and it was mostly just run to the end of the map, picking off common here or there. There are very few routes to explore and most of the time is spent traveling a straight path to the safe room.

The lack of a PVP style VS mode limits the replayability for me but at the price point of the game this may not be an issue, and for anyone looking for co-op game, they seem to have content for you in mind. User created campaigns and mods being added make me hopeful for the co-op staying fresh for a while.

If you love Left 4 Dead, then you will love this. However, I cannot recommend it just yet at its current state. If want to buy this game, it's purely to support the developers and help beta test their game. I'm leaving this as positive because I had more fun with this game than I did with back4blood.
Paid $30 for this when it first came out, dropped to $9.99 USD, this game may not even be worth your time for free..

It's a decent game overall. Aims in a very funky-disco style with nice use of colors & sounds!

[b]However[/b], it still feels a lot generic in some aspects. To be very short and direct; the guns don't feel much of a difference using in terms of damage and sound. Am I using a good gun? Is it really doing damage? Ragolls is another part of the issue. Sometimes the dying animation takes a bit time to kick in and it falls on the ground in a "funny" way, not very smoothly. The amount of specials aliens is lacking a bit. The big one simply rushes at you with no other animation or variation. The goo one and the rolling guys who deploy later are the good ones. I liked them! Now, the "flashy guy" who brights the whole room is the most annoying. Thank god there is an option to reduce it but I'd choose, I'd scrap him completely.

The horde feels weird - sometimes it spawns a lot and you can't think through (one of my friends complained about performance on an Intel); other spawns a nice decent amount. They could also have a better AI to walk in different directions or predict your next move, not always going in a straight line. Also, going through maps/episodes doesn't feel rewarding enough. I'm not sure how this could be improved so it's up in the air and to others. Lastly, let us host our own local servers so we don't need to relay on official dedicated servers to play.

----------------------------------------------

I've read other (negative) reviews and they have pointed out a lot of nice issues that could be looked into during the early access period. I would [b]NOT[/b] recommend on current price/state but for the fun experience in the free to play weekend and still looking forward to the future I do! I wish good luck to the dev team!
Bad but not because of the disco.

Got to play this whilst it was free, and glad that I did. I don't think this is a game I'd be willing to drop money on yet.

I like the general vibe of the game, but think the implementation needs some work. The art style works in its favour, but the setting doesn't. The weapons don't feel like they have any real weight and nor do the enemies. There are dead ends to go down that give little in the way of reward. There's a perk system, but you choose from three random perks under pressure whilst potentially still being attacked by enemies.

The game would benefit from an upgrade system similar to Back 4 Blood, so there'd be at least a reason to go down into corridors to pick up resources. Otherwise levels feel completely lifeless at the moment apart from enemies.

The enemies have a suitably alien design, but the category of enemies are basically a direct copy from Left 4 Dead and Back 4 Blood.

Basically, it's L4D in space, but not quite nailing the execution as well... at least not yet.

At first when I tried this game during the free-weekend period, I was very, VERY skeptical about it. But after playing more of it, I was able to fully experience what the game had to offer (so far)! 
The Anacrusis is a fantastic co-op shooter with a twist of 60's retro future vibes! The gameplay is spectacular, the characters are interesting to learn about, etc. I would write a full review of this game, but I'll save that until the game fully releases. Keep in mind that this isn't L4D, no co-op shooter will ever over succeed L4D. Also if you are planning on buying it, get it during the sale.

It's L4D in disco space. Pretty fun. Quite rough around the edges still.
That said it's worth a play at the price point I'm seeing, especially if you enjoy the style and quality of visuals on offer; the game is a real looker.
The matchmaking worked fine, and the server wasn't bad but felt like it was out of my region which has its downsides; that said it felt great for an out of region server. The game also has swift and flexible AFK mechanics - essentially cribbed from L4D - but the fact that they're in there is important. If you're going to copy; copy the good stuff.
While all the sounds are great, and the soundtrack is amazing, the audio mix is not great. Sound distance is hard to judge and there aren't audible sound cues for important things like footsteps and if mobs are hitting you, immersion is hard to establish because of this. Also the score consistently drowns out the SFX, which is not okay outside of crescendo events.
The guns all have their place. The game is mechanically paced quite well. The first episode is 1h30, the second is 0h30, there is not and should be an indicator of how long each episode is expected to be.
3 of us got stuck in a wall at one time and the solution for the ones who could not wiggle out was to let yourself AFK, then have the bot that takes you over teleport to your team mates.
There are novel mechanics in the game, but I don't know how worth talking about they are when there are still issues with basic interactions, moment to moment loops, and immersion. I will update my views here later on if they develop.

I don't often find myself wanting to revisit games with such a lack of content but Anacrusis' core gameplay is just too good. This game really captures the spirit of L4D in a fresh and exciting way. Mowing down hordes of alien zombies is just so damn satisfying. 

The game, however, falls a little flat in terms of variety. You could play through the entire content offering TWICE in about 3 hours and you'll have seen everything the game has to offer. Even the powerups feel a little stale after a while.

Austin Powers plays Left4Dead in Spaaaaace disco bonanza Electric Bogaloo

While the looks are mostly funky, the rest of the game feels flat at the moment.

Gunplay is pew-pew-pew without any kick. Pistol shoots like a BB gun.

Enemies are mostly L4D template - grunt, tank, puker, grabber, etc. 

Weapons are bland - smg, assault rifle, shotgun with some specials like laser cannon and tesla gun, which have low amount of ammo so their usability is very low. Headshots feels like... well they don't feel like anything at all now.

What's nice is the perk generator machine which gives you a choice between 3 perks that modify this or that in a small way (like better shotgun blasts, better grenade range, faster push recharge, etc.). It's a nice concept but not a game changer now.

You cannot play solo to get to know maps, that is a minus for me.

Music is mostly generic, I did not feel any vibe to it.

In conclusion - at this moment I cannot recommend the game. Maybe after 6 months of additional dev work there would be some improvements but right now even the old L4D2 beats this game by leagues.

reviews.review:
Oh look, it's yet another developer that tries to make another Left 4 Dead clone, but apparently never actually played the game or understand why they're such fun, timeless games. Left 4 Dead offered satisfying weapons and combat, unique locales, a specific and unique atmosphere and environments for each campaign, all of which appeared once-lived-in, abandoned, and falling apart. It had thrilling / exciting / suspenseful music that fit the current situation, likable characters with very unique, specific personalities, attitudes and clothes / character design that regardless of where you were, they stuck out distinctly. The specials always stuck out and were immediately recognizable. Nothing "blended together", but everything fit perfectly and complimented eachother to create a unique and highly functional, immersive experience.

This game, and games like Back 4 Blood and Earthfall have absolutely none of that.

The characters aren't interesting, they have no personality, the only thing unique about them is their physical appearance and their voice. The weapons are boring and uninteresting, the enemies are much the same as well. There's no build up, suspense, tension, the levels are just pristine, vibrant yet forgettable set pieces with a smattering of "damage" here and there. They don't look lived in, the only indication that anyone might've actually lived there is the destroyed robots that are absolutely definitely not HELPER from Venture Bros.

Some might say "B-b-b-ut early access!!" If your game is early access, then what it's missing is content like levels, guns, mechanics, etc. The core feel and vision is there and complete. It is what it is, and it's lacking life and personality outside of a "pretty 70's aesthetic". Everything blends together in a bad way. There was one part in the first campaign, where you go "outside" into the park, and if you look up, you see the sky, but the sky is flickering / cracked because it's a damaged screen / ceiling. *That* was a cool effect though, I will admit that.

I want a GOOD left 4 dead clone more than anyone, but this game is shaping up to be Earthfall 2. It's an interesting concept visually, but the longevity isn't there.

If you want an example of how to do a Left 4 Dead style game well, look at World War Z, or even better, Vermintide 2. Because unfortunately, that's all we've got.
